ledger.note: 367: the Duchy of East Zhou breaks away from Western Zhou. 'Duke Hui of Western Zhou succeeded his father, Duke Wei, in 367 BC'; his younger brother Prince Gen 'occupied eastern part of the state and revolted against Duke Hui', and with help from Zhao and Han Eastern Zhou 'won independence from Western Zhou' (infobox 'Independence from Western Zhou: 367 BCE').

wars.outcome: Qin annexed East Zhou in 249 BC, 58 years after it became a Qin vassal (307) and seven years after the king of Zhou's submission in 256 (eastern-zhou dossier).
wars.note: The page is silent on 256 and 251 and names no battle: the two duchies 'attacked on each other'. The eastern-zhou dossier (ea-01-d) writes that the remnant 'was defeated in 251 and 249 BC' from a page not opened here; this page dates only 249, so 251 is not used.

certainty.note: No East Zhou boundary is on the page; a county-sized duchy. Soft throughout.

notes: Page opened (1 of 1-2): Eastern Zhou (state). Wikidata id left null (unreachable). SLUG east-zhou is the form the qin and eastern-zhou dossiers already use as counterpart. THE DATES DISAGREE across dossiers: eastern-zhou (ea-01-d) writes a 'split' at 314 (page silent, inferred from the capital move) and ends at 256; this page gives 367 for the split and 249 for the annexation, so the eastern-zhou ledger's 314 event should be moved to 367 and its note on the 251/249 remnant now has a dossier. The Western Zhou duchy (Wangcheng) is the eastern-zhou dossier's own state; no separate west-zhou dossier is written. Qin vassalage over East Zhou since 307 is a qin-ledger event (vassal_start, counterpart east-zhou), absent from the qin dossier. AREA: none on the page. Rulers: Duke Hui 367-360, Duke Wu (no reign), Lord Zhaowen (no reign, disputed): no ruler strip. The Western Zhou (state) page was not opened.
